title: Customer Review Deck Orchestrator — standard + enterprise variants
content:
Purpose and usage: This slide-set is a flexible, speaker-note-heavy template for Customer Success teams running QBR-style customer reviews and renewal conversations. Two parallel paths are included: a lightweight Standard flow for product-led/mid-market accounts and an expanded Enterprise flow for strategic, multi-stakeholder renewals. Use the Standard flow when the ask is adoption / expansion and the customer has low contractual complexity. Use the Enterprise flow when there are SLA/contract discussions, multi-team technical migration plans, or finance procurement milestones.

Slide 1 — Title + One-line outcome
- Title: Customer Review — [Account Name], [Quarter]
- One-line outcome (speaker note): State the meeting objective up-front (e.g., align on value delivered, confirm renewal posture, identify 60–90d expansion opportunities).

Slide 2 — Executive snapshot (1 slide for execs)
- Top-left: 1-line health (Green/Yellow/Red) with short rationale.
- Top-right: Renewal window and ARR/subscription cadence.
- Bottom: Top 3 outcomes we want from this meeting.
- Speaker notes: For execs, keep it <3 minutes; highlight ROI, risk, and clear asks.

Slide 3 — Adoption & usage trends (metrics-focused)
- Charts to prepare: weekly active routes, average latency p50/p95, tokens per session, API error rate, 90/7/1 day usage trend.
- Standard variant: Emphasize end-user features and growth signals (new teams onboarded, feature adoption).
- Enterprise variant: Include per-environment throughput, dedicated capacity utilization, and incident/uptime summary.
- Speaker notes: Bring concrete examples tied to business outcomes — e.g., how lower latency improved conversion.

Slide 4 — Health signals and trigger matrix
- Table of signals: adoption velocity, latency variance, cost per 1k tokens, open support tickets, unresolved security items.
- Trigger guidance: green=open, yellow=engage CSM, red=escalate to solutions engineering.
- Speaker notes: Use this to drive next-step recommendations (risk mitigation or expansion play).

Slide 5 — Value stories (customer narratives)
- 2–3 short customer-specific anecdotes: feature X enabled Y outcome (metric + quote).
- Standard: Pull 2 product-led wins. Enterprise: Add a technical win that reduced infra cost or simplified deployment.

Slide 6 — Renewal posture and ask ladder
- Renewal status: Not started / In progress / Confirmed.
- Ask ladder (3 tiers): Upsell (value-led), Renew at base, Enterprise renewal + SLA add-ons.
- Speaker notes: Present options succinctly and recommend a preferred path. Provide timelines and approval owners.

Slide 7 — Risk & mitigation plan (enterprise-heavy)
- Risk vector heatmap (people, tech, finance, compliance).
- Mitigations: escrow, trial periods for new models, dedicated support hours, regional hosting options.
- Speaker notes: Assign owners and short due-dates for top 2 risks.

Slide 8 — 6-week renewal sprint (playbook)
- Week 0–1: Executive alignment + confirm decision criteria.
- Week 2–3: Technical deep-dive and POC verification (if needed).
- Week 4: Commercial proposal and negotiation window opens.
- Week 5: Final approvals and contract prep.
- Week 6: Renewal close + kickoff for next-term success plan.
- Speaker notes: Call out dependent internal tickets (sales opp id, procurement lead) and required artifacts.

Slide 9 — Enterprise addendum: SLA / security checklist
- Items: uptime targets, incident response times, audit log retention, encryption at rest/in transit, SOC/ISO reports.
- Optional contractual tabs: penalty lanes, credits, dedicated capacity clause.
- Speaker notes: Share legal/compliance contacts to expedite procurement reviews.

Slide 10 — Commercial summary and #s (two variants)
- Standard: baseline ARR, recommended expansion, offer window discount, renewal date.
- Enterprise: line items for dedicated capacity, premium support, audit package, expected ROI.
- Speaker notes: Prepare a simple one-page price table and a 30/60/90 day impact forecast.

Slide 11 — Next steps & owners (clear commitments)
- For each action include owner, due date, and required artifacts. Keep to 5 or fewer items.

Appendix A — One-page technical snapshot (for SRE/infra)
- Endpoint list, region, model variants in use, KV cache hit rate, typical batch sizes.
- Speaker notes: Attach a short runbook for SRE handoff if migration is planned.

Appendix B — Renewal tracker sample (text table)
- Columns: Item | Owner | Status | Due | Blockers
- Example row: Commercial proposal | Marcus (AM) | In progress | 2026-03-25 | Legal needs NDA
- Guidance: Keep tracker public in a shared Google Sheet and link in the deck.

Appendix C — Suggested slide timings and choreography
- 0–3 min: Exec snapshot and outcomes
- 3–10 min: Adoption metrics and value stories
- 10–18 min: Risk, SLA, and technical deep dive (if requested)
- 18–25 min: Commercial ask and closing motion
- 25–30 min: Q&A and wrap

Speaker note conventions and delivery tips:
- Use quantifiable numbers wherever possible. If you can’t show exact ARR, show percentage uplift or engagement deltas.
- Bring a single one-page leave-behind that summarizes the executive snapshot and the ask ladder.
- For enterprise customers, always have legal and solutions engineering on standby for follow-up.

Customization checklist (before the meeting):
- Replace placeholders with account-specific stats and names.
- Validate performance numbers with Observability/Console exports.
- Confirm renewal window and procurement timeline with AM / Sales.
- Attach the shared renewal tracker and the last 3 support tickets relevant to the decision.

Notes and common pitfalls observed in field drafts:
- Overloading slides with raw logs — use summaries and links to deeper artifacts.
- Using product-speak rather than business outcomes. Reframe latency and token cost as user conversion / cost per user.
- Missing decision owner — always close each action with a single named owner.

Quick templates (copy-paste slides):
- Exec snapshot: [Health] [Renewal window] [Top 3 meeting outcomes]
- Ask ladder: [Renew | Renew + support | Expand to enterprise plan] with bullet of benefits for each tier.
- Risk mitigation summary: [Risk] -> [Owner] -> [Mitigation] -> [Due]

Linked references to include when finalizing deck:
- Link to renewal tracker sheet, last QBR notes, recent incident postmortems, SRE runbook, procurement checklist.

If you use this in practice: save a copy per account, populate the appendix tables, tag the sheet with the sales opportunity id, and set a follow-up task in the CRM for 3 days post-meeting.

Revision history: v0.1 initial draft by Sophie Martinez; v0.2 added enterprise SLA checklist and 6-week sprint by Ethan Brooks; this is v0.3 with sample tracker row and delivery notes (2026-03-10).
